thread:
sara (support): :rotating_light: Customer 'AcmeFin' reports spikes of 502/504s hitting /v1/generate since ~09:12 UTC. They see timeouts and errors in our hosted API. Attaching sample request/response they sent.

customer-ops: here's their curl and response:

``
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"short prompt"}' -v
> HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
> content-type: application/json
> {"error":"gateway_timeout","message":"upstream timed out contacting cache/kv"}
```

sara (support): They say it was ~40% of requests failing, p95 latency shot to >3s. Happened across eu-west and us-west pools.

ops-bot: Alert: redis-cache-cluster-prod experienced high error rate starting 2026-03-15T09:11:24Z. ERR: connection refused / read timeout. PagerDuty: paging oncall.

miguel (infra): I'm seeing a correlated surge of socket errors from runtime -> prefix-cache (redis). Connection timeouts, then retries. Logs:
``
ERROR runtime.proxy kv/get prefix:RPC failed: dial tcp 10.4.12.8:6379: i/o timeout
WARN prefix-cache: retry limit reached for key="users/123/prefix"
```

kevin (runtime-eng): Could be new eviction pressure after yesterday's traffic change. Any config drift on redis side? AOF/replica promotion? Also saw `READONLY You can't write against a read only replica` in a small subset.

miguel (infra): Confirmed a partial failover happened while a rolling patch ran on the redis primary set in eu-west. Some replicas were briefly promoted, but clients still had pinned addresses and got `READONLY` and TCP resets.

jaz (oncall-sre): Immediate mitigation options:
- flip per-tenant fallback to "no-prefix-cache" for hosted API (bypass kv reads)
- increase runtime cache client timeouts and reduce retries
- route traffic to dedicated pools that don't use prefix caching
Which should we do first?

kevin (runtime-eng): Best first step: disable prefix caching for all hosted generate endpoints for affected regions (eu-west then us-west) to stop runtime blocking on kv. That will increase token cost but keep customers online. I can push a rollout with a canary in 2 mins.

sara (support): I'll patch the support ticket and notify affected customers of mitigation plan. Set expectations about temporary cost/latency hit.

miguel (infra): I'll confirm redis cluster health and rollback failed patch if needed. If we can restore stable primaries we can re-enable cache later.

jaz (oncall-sre): On it. Rolling config now: `route.prefetch.prefix_cache=false` for region=eu-west. Canary on 5% traffic.

ops-bot: Deploy job started: roll-config 9482 by jaz

customer-ops: Can you provide a repro we can run internally to validate the bypass?

kevin (runtime-eng): Repro steps for QA:
1) hit /v1/generate with header `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west` and body model=redwood-1-large
2) observe 502s pre-mitigation; after bypass, check that responses return 200 but token latency p50 increases ~30-40ms.
Commands:
``
# simulate user
for i in {1..20}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST' -H 'X-Redwood-Region: eu-west' -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"hi"}' | jq -r '.error'; done
```

miguel (infra): eu-west redis cluster shows primary down and automatic failover triggered but client DNS TTL was long. We're forcing a failover fix and will rotate clients to new endpoints.

ops-bot: Redis cluster restore progress: 30% complete (syncing replicas)

jaz (oncall-sre): Canary looks good at 5% -> rolling to 50%. Errors in logs drop from 42% -> 2%.

sara (support): Customers on the ticket confirming errors dropping. Putting an interim status update now.

kevin (runtime-eng): After rolling to 100% for eu-west, plan to repeat for us-west. Also scheduling a code change to tolerate READONLY responses by auto-bypassing writes to cache and degrading gracefully.

miguel (infra): Patched a TTL for client-side cluster discovery from 15m -> 30s to avoid pinned addresses in failover. Will monitor.

ops-bot: Post-incident check: api 502 errors normalized. Remaining items: root cause postmortem, alert tuning, and support messaging.

sara (support): Filing follow-up: ensure support bundle includes sample request/response, customer latency graphs, and timeline. Assign to kevin+miguel for RCA.

kevin (runtime-eng): I'll own the runtime change and a canary for READONLY handling. Miguel, can you add a postmortem section about the rolling patch and failover sequence?

miguel (infra): Yep. Adding timeline and redis logs to the incident doc.

jaz (oncall-sre): Closing the immediate SEV. If anything reappears we re-open. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

customer-ops: Thank you team — confirmed service restored on our side.
